headings.title: Definitions for this section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(5)) and section history note (L. 1988 S.B. 600 through A.L. 2008 S.B. 931). Defines 'fuel ethanol', 'fuel ethanol blends', 'Missouri qualified fuel ethanol producer', 'professional forester', and 'qualified biomass' solely for section 142.028. Note that adjacent unnumbered section 142.029 specifies a December 31, 2015 expiration date for section 142.028; this heading describes the archived text without claiming current enforceability.

headings.title: Incentive fund creation, purpose, and administration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Creates the Missouri Qualified Fuel Ethanol Producer Incentive Fund to provide economic subsidies subject to appropriations and assigns fund administration to the director of the department of agriculture.

headings.title: Monthly grant eligibility, calculation, payment, and adjustments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers the 60-month eligibility cap (and conditional extension up to 24 additional months for appropriation shortfalls), per-gallon incentive tiers (20 cents for the first 12.5 million gallons and 5 cents for the next 12.5 million gallons per fiscal year, with production over 25 million gallons excluded) for Missouri agricultural products or qualified biomass, payment within 15 days after application receipt and approval, and subsequent-month reconciliation adjustments when actual production differs from estimates.

headings.title: Monthly grant application deadline and contents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(6)) and history note. Sets the application deadline (15 days prior to the first day of the grant month) and six required content items. Source cross-reference note: subdivision (5) refers to a 'qualified fuel ethanol producer license required pursuant to subsection 5 of this section' alongside bonding under subsection 5, whereas subsection 5 addresses rulemaking and bonding procedures without explicitly referencing a license; retained without altering source text.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority and producer bonding requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs the director of agriculture, in consultation with the departments of revenue and conservation, to promulgate administrative rules and establish bonding procedures, capping required bonds at the estimated maximum monthly grant; does not itself state licensing provisions referenced in subsection 4(5).

headings.title: Rulemaking compliance with chapter 536 and nonseverability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Subjects rules (as defined in section 536.010) created under this section to chapter 536 and, if applicable, section 536.028, declares nonseverability with chapter 536, and voids the rulemaking grant and post-August 28, 2002 rules if legislative review powers under chapter 536 are held unconstitutional.

headings.title: Limits and eligibility window for biomass ethanol subsidies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note (A.L. 2008 S.B. 931). Caps qualified-biomass fuel ethanol subsidies from January 1, 2009 through December 31, 2019 at two producers and $7.5 million cumulatively per producer, and declares biomass ethanol producers ineligible before January 1, 2009 and after December 31, 2019. Source caveat: adjacent unnumbered section 142.029 states that section 142.028 expires December 31, 2015, which precedes this subsection's December 31, 2019 window; heading describes only the archived subsection text.

headings.title: Definitions for this section

headings.title: Topics for analysis and recommendations

headings.title: Base tax rates, measurement standards, and mixed-use connections

headings.title: Consumer tax incidence and precollection by agents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Declares that all taxes, surcharges, and fees are imposed upon the ultimate consumer and precollected through specified chapter persons acting as state agents.

headings.title: Additional phased motor fuel tax rates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note (A.L. 2021 S.B. 262). Levies additional phased per-gallon motor fuel tax rates from October 1, 2021 (2.5 cents) through July 1, 2025 and after (12.5 cents) in addition to subsection 1(1), explicitly subject to the tax liability exemption in section 142.822.

headings.title: Presumption for fuel delivered into vehicle supply tanks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Establishes a highway-use presumption for motor fuel delivered in Missouri into a motor vehicle fuel supply tank, qualified by the exception in section 142.815(2)(6).

headings.title: Presumption for terminal removals, imports, and bulk tanks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history note. Establishes a highway-use presumption, subject to proof of exemption under section 142.815, for fuel removed from an in-state terminal, imported outside a bulk transfer in the bulk transfer/terminal system, or delivered into a consumer's bulk storage tank from which motor vehicles can be fueled.

headings.title: Timing and measurement for non-bulk-transfer fuel imports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Specifies when tax arises on motor fuel imported other than by bulk transfer and measures it by invoiced gallons received out-of-state, or by actual gallons imported if exceeding both net and gross gallons on shipping papers.

headings.title: Measurement for terminal-system removals and non-supplier sales
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history note. Except as in subsection 1, measures tax by invoiced gallons removed (other than by bulk transfer) from an in-state bulk transfer/terminal system, an out-of-state system for Missouri delivery by an importing supplier or under a section 142.839 election, or upon sale in an in-state terminal or refinery to a person without a supplier's license. headings.title: Measurement of alcohol, blend stocks, and blended fuel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Applies subsection 2(1) to imported blend fuels and subsection 2(2) to fuel grade alcohol and blend stocks imported into a terminal even by other than a bulk transfer.

headings.title: Annual excise tax and terminal loss calculation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Imposes an annual excise tax at the motor fuel rate on unaccounted-for terminal losses exceeding 0.5% of net gallons removed during the calendar year, and sets the inventory-and-receipts minus ending-inventory-and-removals calculation formula.

headings.title: Terminal operator liability, presumption, and substantiation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes the terminal operator liable for the section's tax, presumes received fuel not reported as removed is unaccounted for, and permits documentation to substantiate unaccountable losses.

headings.title: Nonhighway fuel exemptions and consumer or vendor refunds

headings.title: Additional tax exemptions and deduction or refund procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(9), including paragraphs (a)–(c) of subdivisions (1) and (8)) and history note. headings.title: Fiscal-year exemption and refund for section 142.803(3) tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2021 S.B. 262). headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(6)) and history note. headings.title: Three-year recordkeeping requirement for claimants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires every person filing a claim statement to maintain supporting records, invoices, original sales receipts marked paid, bills of lading, and director-required papers for three years.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') for the director to investigate exemption and refund claims both before issuance and afterward within chapter tax-adjustment time frames.

headings.title: Interest on delayed refunds after forty-five days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires interest at the section 32.065 rate if an exemption and refund is not issued within 45 days after an accurate and complete filing.

headings.title: Vehicle gross weight eligibility limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Limits section 142.822 exemptions and refunds to motor fuel delivered into motor vehicles with a gross weight (as defined in section 301.010) of 26,000 pounds or less.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority, chapter 536 compliance, and nonseverability

headings.title: Claims when original sales slip or invoice is lost
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires an explanatory statement and invoice serial number when an original sales slip or invoice is lost or destroyed, giving the director permissive authority ('may') to allow an otherwise regular claim.

headings.title: Pre-refund and post-refund director investigations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants permissive authority to investigate motor fuel tax refund claims before issuance and afterward within chapter tax-adjustment time frames.

headings.title: Supplier credit in lieu of refund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits a supplier to claim a credit in lieu of a payable chapter refund for a period not exceeding three years.

headings.title: Three-year recordkeeping requirement for refund claims
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires every person to maintain substantiating records, invoices, original sales slips marked paid, bills of lading, and director-required papers for three years.

headings.title: Refund of motor fuel tax paid more than once
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Directs refund of duplicate motor fuel tax paid on the same gallon to the person who last paid after the subsequent taxable event, conditional on proof satisfactory to the director.

headings.title: Refund of other erroneously paid motor fuel tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 6 by covering motor fuel tax otherwise erroneously paid, refundable upon proof satisfactory to the director.

headings.title: Interest on delayed refunds after forty-five days
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Requires interest at the section 32.065 rate accruing after 45 days if a refund is not issued within 45 days of an accurate and complete filing.

headings.title: Distributor invoices for lake-county marina and boat-fuel deliveries

headings.title: Annual calculation and distribution of unclaimed boat-fuel refunds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. headings.title: County refund expenditure limits and lake-access road transfers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. headings.title: Filing notice of election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Specifies that the section 142.839 election is made by filing a 'notice of election' with the director.

headings.title: Published list of electing suppliers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the director to publish a list of suppliers making an election under section 142.839.

headings.title: Continuing tax responsibility without an election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Clarifies that not making a blanket election does not relieve a supplier from remitting chapter tax on out-of-state terminal removals imported into Missouri by the supplier.

headings.title: Precollection duty of electing suppliers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. headings.title: Jurisdictional defense waiver by electing suppliers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Provides that electing suppliers waive any defense that Missouri lacks jurisdiction to require tax collection on out-of-state sales known to be destined for Missouri under the state's general police powers.

headings.title: Penalty relief and liability agreements for fuel diversions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. headings.title: Precollection and remittance on in-state terminal or refinery removals

headings.title: Separate invoice line item for tax

headings.title: Supplier tax payment due date
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Makes supplier tax for a calendar month's removals due on or before the second day of the second succeeding month, or the next succeeding business day if that date falls on a weekend or state holiday.

headings.title: Remittance and notice of late eligible-purchaser payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires suppliers to remit late taxes paid by eligible purchasers and timely notify the director if the supplier previously gave nonreceipt notice under section 142.857(1).

headings.title: Basis of remittance amounts and electronic funds transfer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Bases remittances on invoiced amounts for eligible purchasers or 97% (gasoline, blends, blend stocks) and 98% (diesel, blends, blend stocks) for a supplier's own account or noneligible purchasers, and allows electronic funds transfer at the director's discretion.

headings.title: Eligibility evidence for section 142.848 election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Requires a purchaser seeking a section 142.848 timing election to show either good-standing tax-remitting licensee status under the predecessor statute or compliance with chapter financial responsibility and section-conforming bonding requirements.

headings.title: Surety bond or security and credit indemnification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes the director to require a surety bond or financial security up to three times monthly potential tax payments (capped at $150,000 separately for gasoline and diesel) and indemnification against supplier tax credits under section 142.854.

headings.title: Bonding exemption and transition for pre-1999 licensed distributors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Exempts licensed distributors meeting pre-effective-date bonding laws from subsection 2, and preserves the historical January 1, 1999 transition allowing pre-1999 licensed distributors to elect eligible purchaser status and use section 142.896 distributor bonding.

headings.title: Rescinding eligibility, restoration conditions, and administrative review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes rescinding a purchaser's deferral eligibility upon untimely section 142.848 payment (via supplier notice or publication), allows uncapped increased-bond or other conditions for restoration, and permits Administrative Hearing Commission review while prohibiting stays.

headings.title: Published list of eligible purchasers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires the director to publish a list of eligible purchasers and make it available to all suppliers.

headings.title: Eligibility, notice, limits, and reinstatement for section 142.854 credit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and source notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99; source footnote '*Word "the" does not appear in original rolls.' on 'failure to collect the* tax'). Governs the 10-business-day notice requirement for section 142.854 supplier credits, evidence and defaulting-purchaser identification, first-return claiming deadline, credit cap (unpaid amount plus up to 10 days or notice date), and bar on additional credit until the director notifies the supplier that the purchaser's section 142.851 eligibility is restored.

headings.title: Destination-state tax defaults and dual-capacity collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Raises the section 142.806 Missouri-use presumption when a supplier credit stems from unpaid destination-state tax on section 142.815(2)(1) export shipments, and directs the director to seek payment in a dual capacity for both Missouri and the destination state.

headings.title: Termination of destination-state credits upon reciprocity agreement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Terminates section 142.857's credits for unpaid destination-state motor fuel taxes once the director enters a collection reciprocity agreement with authorized representatives of that state.

headings.title: Consumer liability when motor fuel tax is not precollected
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Holds the ultimate consumer liable for unprecollected section 142.803 tax on highway motor fuel delivered into a vehicle fuel supply tank (unless exempted under section 142.869 or section 142.815(2)(3) and (5)), including dyed diesel fuel and fuel on which a refund claim has been made.

headings.title: Conditional joint and several liability of ultimate vendors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes an ultimate vendor (other than a federally recognized Indian tribe) jointly and severally liable for the subsection 1 backup tax if the vendor knows or has reason to know the untaxed fuel is or will be consumed in a nonexempt use.

headings.title: Annual decal fee schedule, exemptions, and plug-in hybrid definition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619 through A.L. 2021 S.B. 262). Exempts Missouri-registered decal-bearing alternative-fuel vehicles from chapter tax (while taxing non-subsection-4 propane, CNG, and LNG exclusively under section 142.803(1)(4)–(7)), establishes weight/farm/passenger annual fee tiers and half-fees for plug-in electric hybrids, exempts section 301.131 historic vehicles from both tax and decals, and defines 2018-or-newer unmodified plug-in electric hybrids.

headings.title: Five-year phased annual decal fee increases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (A.L. 2021 S.B. 262). Increases subsection 1 fees annually for five years beginning January 1, 2022 by 20% of August 28, 2021 fees, except vehicles over 36,000 pounds licensed gross weight increase by 10% per year for five years.

headings.title: Temporary decals for out-of-state alternative-fuel vehicles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides $8, 15-day nontransferable windshield decals in lieu of section 142.803 tax for out-of-state alternative-fuel vehicles (excluding interstate users, section 142.617 reciprocity vehicles, and propane/CNG/LNG vehicles), directs section 142.345 deposit of proceeds, and allows dealers 50 cents retention for timely remittance.

headings.title: Grandfathered CNG and LNG decals for private-station owners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Allows owners/operators of pre-December 31, 2015 private CNG/LNG stations serving only their own vehicles to continue using vehicle decals in lieu of section 142.803(1)(4)–(5) taxes, bars sales to non-owned vehicles, ends eligibility if decals are not renewed after January 1, 2016, and taxes CNG/LNG obtained at non-owned stations. Revised during review to clarify decals apply to vehicles of private-station owners rather than the stations themselves.

headings.title: Propane vehicle decals and tax collection at fueling stations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Permits propane vehicle decals in lieu of section 142.803(1)(6) tax, permits quick-connect station operators collecting tax to sell without verifying decals, and bars refunds when decal-bearing propane vehicles refuel at unattended stations.

headings.title: Annual fee collection, proration, and unattended propane exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Sets January 31 annual collection, department application forms, 1/12 monthly proration for vehicles not in operation by January 31, and an exception for propane vehicles fueled exclusively at tax-collecting unattended stations.

headings.title: Decal issuance, calendar-year validity, and windshield display
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Directs decal issuance upon subsection 1 fee payment, sets calendar-year validity, and requires attachment to the lower right-hand corner of the front windshield.

headings.title: Decal fee transfers upon ownership change or equipment reinstallation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Makes subsection 1 decal fees transferable upon a change of ownership of the motor vehicle or upon removing LP gas or natural gas equipment upon a change of ownership and reinstalling it in another vehicle, in accordance with director rules. Revised during review to preserve 'ownership change' rather than narrowing to 'sale'.

headings.title: Operating without a required decal and fueling-station exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Prohibits highway operation of a vehicle required to have an alternative fuel decal without a valid decal, subject to the express exception for vehicles exclusively fueled at tax-collecting propane, CNG, or LNG stations. Revised during review to surface the fueling-station exception rather than presenting the prohibition as unconditional.

headings.title: Prohibition on fueling vehicles lacking a decal or tax collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Prohibits placing alternative fuel into the fuel supply receptacle or battery of a vehicle required to have a decal unless a valid decal is attached or appropriate fuel tax is collected at fueling.

headings.title: Infraction classification and fine for violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Classifies any violation of section 142.869 as an infraction punishable by a $500 fine upon conviction.

headings.title: Exemption from chapter licensing and reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Exempts motor vehicles displaying a valid alternative fuel decal from chapter 142 licensing and reporting requirements.

headings.title: In-state terminal removals diverted from export to Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Requires distributors diverting in-state terminal export shipments into Missouri to notify (including section 142.917 compliance) and pay section 142.803 tax under section 142.836 terms, shields precollecting suppliers from civil penalties/interest on diversion corrections, allows mutual supplier-distributor liability assumption agreements, and leaves exporters liable for accrued interest and penalties.

headings.title: Refund for tax-paid fuel exported from in-state bulk plant
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Entitles an exporter removing previously taxed or tax-accrued motor fuel from an in-state bulk plant for export to a refund upon proof of export satisfactory to the director.

headings.title: Out-of-state terminal removals diverted into Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires importers diverting out-of-state terminal shipments into Missouri to comply with section 142.917 notice and pay import tax under section 142.836 terms, with an option for a licensed supplier to assume importer liability by mutual agreement.

headings.title: Refunds and supplier credits for legal diversions out of Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs distributors legally diverting Missouri-destined fuel to another state to seek a section 142.815 refund (or assign the claim by mutual agreement for a supplier credit), and allows suppliers a credit for supplier-directed diversions on the supplier's account.

headings.title: Tax-difference adjustments under multistate compacts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Limits diversion payment or refund to the difference in state taxes where a multistate compact applies, upon notice to both states and proof of destination-state payment, and directs the director to set procedures and maintain a qualifying-state list.

headings.title: Final report filing and payment upon business or license end
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 1999 S.B. 414). headings.title: Deemed license termination on January 1, 1999 for non-suppliers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Historical conversion rule deeming pre-January 1, 1999 motor fuel tax remittance licensees not licensed as chapter suppliers to have their licenses terminated as of January 1, 1999.

headings.title: Twelve-month installment payment option for pre-1999 distributors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Historical transition allowing pre-January 1, 1999 distributors lacking section 142.851 eligible purchaser status to pay final-report tax plus section 32.065 interest in director-agreed installments not exceeding 12 months after January 1, 1999.

headings.title: Thirty-six-month bar on eligible purchaser status after deferral
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Bars any person electing subsection 3 installment deferral from claiming section 142.851 eligible purchaser status for 36 months following the election.

headings.title: Pre-1999 eligible purchaser applications and delayed collection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Grants former licensees an opportunity to apply under sections 142.848 and 142.851 prior to January 1, 1999, delays final-report tax collection pending incomplete determinations, and requires the final report within 30 days after a final denial.

headings.title: Final-month payment and January 1, 1999 conversion notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires final-month liability payment with the final report and notes the section's one-time alternative payment method on January 1, 1999 for converting from the predecessor act.

headings.title: License application form, subscription, and required information
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). headings.title: Applicant investigation and mandatory grounds for license denial
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(9)) and history note. Directs investigation of each applicant and bars issuing a license if any of nine grounds exist (bad faith, non-real party in interest, prior revocation for cause, three unpaid-tax business/control affiliations, director-determined good cause, missing export destination-state license for distributors, or prior motor fuel tax evasion conviction).

headings.title: Applicant fingerprinting, exemptions, FBI processing, and file retention
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. headings.title: Alternative security deposits and bond or letter-of-credit form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Allows cash, certificates of deposit, or irrevocable letters of credit in lieu of required bonds, and requires bonds or letters of credit to use an approved surety/bank (which may be an affiliate), name the applicant as principal obligor and state as obligee, and use director-prescribed forms.

headings.title: Financial statement review, inquiry, and bond increases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Gives the director discretion to require verified financial statements, conduct independent financial inquiries, decline uncertified/unaudited statements as accurate, and require an increased bond if warranted by financial condition.

headings.title: New bond for reduced liability, unsatisfactory surety, and release
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (introductory clause, subdivisions (1)–(2), and continuation sentences) and history note. Authorizes requiring a new bond when prior bond liability is discharged/reduced or a surety becomes unsatisfactory in the director's opinion, requires license cancellation if the new bond is unsatisfactory, and requires written release of the prior surety for post-effective-date liability if satisfactorily furnished. headings.title: Replenishing reduced cash, certificates of deposit, or letters of credit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes requiring a new deposit equal to any reduction when a licensee's cash, certificate of deposit, or letter of credit is reduced by judgment, payment, or other disposition.

headings.title: Demand for new or increased bond if insufficient
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires a licensee, upon written demand after the director reasonably determines an existing bond is insufficient, to file a new or increased bond, granting at least 15 days to secure the increased bond or cash deposit.

headings.title: Chapter compliance for new bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires any new bond to meet the requirements set forth in chapter 142.

headings.title: License cancellation for unsatisfactory new bond
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Directs the director to cancel the license if a new bond required under section 142.881 is unsatisfactory.

headings.title: Surety release from future liability after sixty days' notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Releases a surety from liability accruing more than 60 days after written release request to the director without affecting liability accrued before the 60-day period expires.

headings.title: Licensee notice and replacement bond after surety release request
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires prompt director notice to the licensee of a surety release request and directs license cancellation unless a chapter-compliant new bond is filed within the 60-day period.

headings.title: Cancellation, retention, and replacement of alternative security
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. headings.title: Permissive supplier's license and limited state jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Allows qualifying permissive suppliers wishing to precollect tax to obtain a permissive supplier's license without thereby submitting to Missouri jurisdiction for purposes other than chapter administration and enforcement.

headings.title: Supplier bond amounts and net-worth financial responsibility alternatives

headings.title: Verified supplier statements for precollected tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires every supplier to file verified statements on director-prescribed forms with any reasonably necessary information to determine precollected motor fuel tax due.

headings.title: Disclosing untaxed out-of-state terminal sales destined for Missouri
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. headings.title: Monthly supplier report filing deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Sets the filing deadline for section 142.884 reports on or before the second day of the current month for the second preceding calendar month.

headings.title: Terminal operator's license requirement per site

headings.title: Terminal operator bond calculation and cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires terminal operators to post a bond of at least three months' estimated potential tax liability, capped at $500,000.

headings.title: Monthly sworn statement of in-state terminal operations

headings.title: Licensee inventory recordkeeping

headings.title: Conditional reporting by out-of-state terminal operators

headings.title: Transporter bond calculation and cap

headings.title: Monthly transporter fuel-movement reports

headings.title: Export distributor license, destination-state rule, and bond exclusion

headings.title: Distributor's license for non-terminal cross-border deliveries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires a distributor's license before delivering dyed or undyed motor fuel from another state by transport truck, pipeline, or barge into storage facilities other than a qualified terminal.

headings.title: Requirements for importing fuel without a supplier precollection agreement

headings.title: Distributor's license for blending motor fuel for sale
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires any person blending any motor fuel for sale to obtain a distributor's license.

headings.title: Distributor's license prerequisite for section 142.848 election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Makes holding a distributor's license a prerequisite to making the tax-remittance timing election permitted in section 142.848.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(4) of sub 3) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified non-supplier export distributor licensing, destination-state condition/exception, and retained archived wording ('destination motor fuel tax of this state... with respect to the exports') in sub 1, non-terminal import deliveries in sub 2, four requirements for imports without supplier trustee agreements (including section 142.929 and section 142.836) in sub 3, blending for sale in sub 4, and section 142.848 prerequisite in sub 5. All 5 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Distributor bond calculation and separate fuel caps
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 1999 S.B. 414). Requires distributors to post a bond of at least three months' estimated total liability, capped at $150,000 separately for gasoline and diesel fuel.

headings.title: Bond calculation exclusion for precollected imported fuel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(2)) and history note. Excludes tax on imported nonexempt motor fuel from distributor bond potential-liability calculations when both section 142.839 tax precollection agreements apply and the director determines all border states have adequate terminal reporting.

headings.title: Motor Fuel Bond Trust Fund cash bond option and operation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Permits section 142.851(3) distributors not bonded under the predecessor act to post a bond or join the created Motor Fuel Bond Trust Fund, bars individual distributor claims against the fund, establishes supplier-remitted contributions, min/max suspension/resumption notices, and 90-day delinquency draws without affecting tax liability or other remedies. Source cross-reference note: archived text says 'post the bond as set out in this subsection' although the regular distributor bond is set out in subsection 1; retained explicitly.

headings.title: Pool bond eligibility after three years of compliance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Allows licensed distributors to participate in the pool bond in lieu of other bonds after three consecutive years of director-determined satisfactory tax compliance, requiring at least one year of contributions regardless of whether the pool has reached its maximum.

headings.title: Monthly bond fund activity reports to pool members
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs the director to compile a monthly motor fuel bond fund activity report—including names and license numbers of licensees with claims against them—for pool members.

headings.title: Distributor tax remittance due date and report filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires distributors to remit tax due on the last day of the succeeding month and file director-prescribed reports.

headings.title: Required contents of distributor reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Specifies non-exhaustive information required in licensed distributor reports: imports, exports, blending, fuel receipts, dyed fuel receipts/sales, tax-free undyed kerosene receipts/sales, and transporting fuel or blend stocks for others.

headings.title: Monthly distributor report filing deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 6 by specifying that the section 142.896 report is due on the last day of each month covering the next preceding calendar month.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 8 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(2) of sub 2) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 1999 S.B. 414), and verified all fingerprints. Verified $150,000 separate gasoline/diesel bond caps in sub 1, two-condition precollected-import exclusion (section 142.839 and border-state reporting) in sub 2, Motor Fuel Bond Trust Fund cash bond option and retained source cross-reference ('post the bond as set out in this subsection') in sub 3, three-year compliance pool eligibility in sub 4, monthly pool reports in sub 5, and distinct tax-remittance, report-content, and report-deadline rules in subs 6–8. All 8 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: License issuance and copies for additional business locations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Directs license issuance for the principal place of business upon applicant and bond approval and requires the applicant to make copies for each business location.

headings.title: Duration of license validity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Provides that a license remains valid until suspended, revoked for cause, or cancelled.

headings.title: Nontransferability of licenses and reporting ownership changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Prohibits transferring a license to another person or place of business, deems transferring a majority interest in a business association a transfer to another person, and requires reporting ownership changes except for publicly held business associations.

headings.title: Preservation and display at principal place of business
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires preserving and conspicuously displaying each license at the principal place of business for which it is issued.

headings.title: Displaying license number on fuel conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires chapter licensees to display their license number on the back of any conveyance of motor fuel.

headings.title: License surrender on business change and relocation notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires immediate license surrender upon business discontinuance, sale, transfer, or ownership change, and immediate reporting of any business relocation.

headings.title: Written notice and continuing liability on discontinuance or transfer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 6 by requiring immediate written notice with date and purchaser/transferee name and address, and preserving tax, interest, penalty, and criminal misuse liability accruing prior to license cancellation.

headings.title: Successor tax clearance, purchase-money withholding, and personal liability
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Relieves a successor from predecessor liability upon obtaining a prior no-tax-due statement from the director, requires withholding purchase money until a tax-paid receipt or no-tax certificate is produced, and imposes personal liability for failing to withhold and remit unpaid taxes, interest, and penalties.

headings.title: Free published licensee list with monthly updates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Requires the director to publish without charge a categorized list of all licensees with monthly updates.

headings.title: Three-year transaction recordkeeping and interstate reciprocity extensions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Requires every licensee (including interstate motor fuel users) to retain motor fuel transaction records, invoices, bills of lading, and required papers for three years, or longer for interstate users if required by a reciprocity agreement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 10 subsections and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified issuance and location copies in sub 1, validity duration in sub 2, nontransferability/majority-interest transfer rule and ownership-change reporting (excluding publicly held associations) in sub 3, display rules in subs 4–5, surrender/relocation vs. written notice/continuing liability in subs 6–7, successor clearance/withholding/personal liability in sub 8, free monthly list in sub 9, and three-year recordkeeping with interstate reciprocity extensions in sub 10. All 10 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: License revocation and Administrative Hearing Commission review
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 1999 S.B. 414). Grants permissive authority ('may') to revoke a license for refusing or neglecting chapter or regulation compliance and allows review of the director's decision by the administrative hearing commission.

headings.title: Unlicensed business activity prohibition and civil or criminal penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Prohibits engaging in licensed-required chapter business activities without first obtaining a license, sets a $1,000 civil penalty for negligent violation, and makes knowing violation or knowing aiding and abetting with intent to evade tax a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Civil penalties for failing to file returns or keep records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') to impose a civil penalty of $100 for a first failure to file a required return or retain required records, increasing by $100 for each additional occurrence.

headings.title: Loss of remittance reductions for late reports or payments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires a late monthly report filer or late tax remitter to pay full motor fuel tax without the reductions allowed by subdivision (2) of section 142.836 (unnumbered section) or subsection 5 of section 142.842, in addition to penalties and interest.

headings.title: Penalties and interest for knowing failure to precollect or remit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Holds a supplier, permissive supplier, or distributor who knowingly fails to precollect or timely remit required tax (including under a precollection agreement) liable for uncollected tax, a 5% monthly penalty up to 25%, and section 32.065 interest.

headings.title: Stealing offense for unremitted or fraudulently withheld tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Makes failing to timely pay collected motor fuel tax or fraudulently withholding, appropriating, or using state money the crime of stealing punishable under section 570.030.

headings.title: Fifty-percent penalty for false or fraudulent tax-evasion returns
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Adds 50% of any deficiency plus section 32.065 interest when a person liable for tax files a false or fraudulent return with intent to evade tax. Revised during review to preserve the statutory 'intent to evade' qualification.

headings.title: Civil penalty and interest deposits under section 142.345
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Directs deposit of all chapter civil penalties and interest to the credit of the motor fuel tax fund created in section 142.345.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 8 subsections and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 1999 S.B. 414), and verified all fingerprints. Verified permissive revocation and AHC review in sub 1, unlicensed-activity civil/class A misdemeanor tiers in sub 2, permissive escalating civil penalties in sub 3, loss of unnumbered section 142.836(2) and section 142.842(5) reductions in sub 4, knowing precollection/remittance penalties in sub 5, section 570.030 stealing offense in sub 6, 50% deficiency penalty requiring intent to evade in sub 7, and section 142.345 fund deposit in sub 8. Revised sub 7 title to preserve the 'intent to evade' element and refined sub 4 reviewNote for exact subdivision citation; retained the other 7 titles.

headings.title: Shipping document requirements for refineries, terminals, and bulk plants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(6)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491, Effective 1-01-17). Requires in-state refinery, terminal, and bulk plant operators to prepare and provide drivers with shipping documents listing origin city/state, removal date, gross and net gallons, represented destination state, director-required enforcement data, and supplier/consignee/carrier.

headings.title: Manually prepared shipping papers and service interruption numbers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Permits manual shipping papers when a terminal lacks automation or faces extraordinary unforeseen circumstances, subject to prior written or telephonic notice, 24-hour service interruption authorization numbers (and renewals), and 10-day advance notice before initial use of newly acquired automated printing.

headings.title: Bulk plant exemptions for tank wagons and net-gallon reporting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Exempts in-state bulk plant deliveries into tank wagons for in-state consumer delivery from section 142.911, and exempts in-state bulk plant operators from identifying net gallons on shipping documents.

headings.title: Shipping documents for multi-state split loads
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Permits refinery or terminal operators to load split loads destined for Missouri and other states provided shipping papers designate the destination state for each portion.

headings.title: Posted notice of section 142.914 duties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Requires refinery and terminal operators to post a conspicuous notice near shipping-paper receipt points stating transport operator and supplier duties under section 142.914, subject to optional director format standards.

headings.title: Prohibition on false statements on shipping papers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Prohibits terminal operators from imprinting and suppliers from knowingly permitting false statements on shipping papers for Missouri or substantially similar states, regardless of whether fuel was dyed.

headings.title: Terminal operator tax liability for knowing false statements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Imposes joint and several liability for uncollected chapter taxes on a terminal operator who knowingly imprints a false statement in violation of section 142.911.

headings.title: Supplier joint and several liability for knowing violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 7 by making any supplier who knowingly violates section 142.911 jointly and severally liable with the terminal operator.

headings.title: Class E felony for knowing tax-evasion violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note (A.L. 2014 S.B. 491, Effective 1-01-17). Makes knowingly violating or knowingly aiding and abetting a violation of section 142.911 with intent to evade chapter tax a class E felony.

headings.title: Civil penalties for terminal shipping-paper issuance violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') to assess a $1,000 first-occurrence and $5,000 subsequent-occurrence civil penalty against terminal operators failing chapter shipping-paper issuance requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 10 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(6) of sub 1) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 2014 S.B. 491, Effective 1-01-17), and verified all fingerprints. Verified six shipping-document elements in sub 1, manual papers/24-hour interruption numbers/10-day automation notice in sub 2, bulk-plant tank-wagon and net-gallon exemptions in sub 3, multi-state split loads in sub 4, posted section 142.914 notice in sub 5, false-statement bar and knowing joint/several liabilities in subs 6–8, class E felony for knowing tax-evasion violations in sub 9, and permissive $1,000/$5,000 terminal civil penalties in sub 10. All 10 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Transporter shipping-document duties, diversions, and tank-wagon rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause, subdivisions (1)–(5), and paragraphs (a)–(c) of subdivision (3)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Requires highway fuel transporters to carry shipping documents, permit law enforcement/director inspection and duplication, deliver to the listed destination state unless completing pre-diversion notice, verification number, and paper annotation steps, give a copy to the receiving facility controller, and meet director conditions, while directing regulations for tank-wagon handwritten designations and alternative procedures.

headings.title: Providing shipping documents to delivery facility operators
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires transporters to provide the original or a copy of the terminal-issued shipping document to the retail outlet, bulk plant, or bulk end user storage facility operator receiving delivery.

headings.title: Recipient examination and retention of shipping documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires receiving facility operators to examine and retain terminal-issued shipping documents for 30 days on-site (or at normal billing address if unattended) and three years off-site.

headings.title: Prohibition on knowingly accepting improperly documented deliveries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Bars retail dealers, bulk plant operators, wholesale distributors, and bulk end users from knowingly accepting bulk storage deliveries lacking compliant shipping papers showing Missouri destination or a section 142.917 diversion verification number and sections 142.926 and 142.929 data.

headings.title: Joint and several tax liability for knowing violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Makes any person who knowingly violates or knowingly aids and abets a violation of section 142.914 jointly and severally liable for the tax on the transported or delivered motor fuel.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for vehicle shipping-paper violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Makes a vehicle owner or operator violating sections 142.914, 142.926, and 142.929 guilty of a class B misdemeanor for a first offense and a class A misdemeanor for second and subsequent offenses.

headings.title: Civil penalties for transporting fuel without annotated shipping papers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Requires a $1,000 civil penalty for a first occurrence and $5,000 for each subsequent occurrence of transporting motor fuel without shipping papers annotated as required under sections 142.914, 142.926, and 142.929.

headings.title: Presumptive violation and vehicle or cargo seizure for missing papers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Makes a loaded motor vehicle operator's failure to have proper chapter shipping papers on board once transportation begins presumptive evidence of a violation warranting impoundment and seizure of the vehicle and cargo.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 8 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(5) and paragraphs (a)–(c) of sub 1) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified transporter document, inspection, diversion, delivery-copy, and tank-wagon duties in sub 1, facility-operator document delivery in sub 2, 30-day on-site/3-year off-site retention in sub 3, knowing acceptance bar (citing sections 142.917, 142.926, and 142.929) in sub 4, knowing joint/several tax liability in sub 5, class B/A misdemeanor escalation and $1,000/$5,000 mandatory civil penalties in subs 6–7, and presumptive violation/seizure in sub 8. All 8 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Rulemaking for diverted shipment and shipping-paper error relief
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Directs promulgation of relief rules when a motor fuel shipment is legitimately diverted after shipping-paper issuance or when a terminal operator fails to print proper information.

headings.title: Prior notice, verification numbers, and refund consistency
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires relief rules to mandate advance notification of intended diversions or corrections, assignment and manual entry of a verification number on the terminal-issued shipping paper, and consistency with chapter refund provisions 'including section 142.845'. Source cross-reference note: archived text cites section 142.845 (which governs terminal operator tax liability rather than refunds); retained verbatim without editing source text.

headings.title: Protest procedure and honest-error defense to civil penalties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires a protest procedure allowing persons found violating section 142.911 and section 142.914(3) to establish a civil-penalty defense via substantial evidence of honest error within a good-faith, reasonable compliance effort.

headings.title: Toll-free diversion reporting and multistate system coordination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs the director to provide toll-free telephone service for diversion reports and verification numbers and to make reasonable efforts to coordinate a shared multistate telephonic assignment system with neighboring states and the Federation of Tax Administrators.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified diversion/error relief rulemaking in sub 1, advance notice/verification number and retained source cross-reference to section 142.845 (verified in archive as terminal-operator tax liability rather than refunds) in sub 2, protest and substantial-evidence honest-error defense for section 142.911 and section 142.914(3) in sub 3, and toll-free telephone service and multistate/FTA coordination in sub 4. All 4 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Prohibition on dealing in or importing untaxed motor fuel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Subject to subsection 2 exceptions, prohibits selling, using, delivering, storing, or importing motor fuel for which section 142.803 tax has not been previously paid to or accrued by a licensed supplier/permissive supplier at terminal removal or a licensed distributor meeting section 142.929 import conditions.

headings.title: Exceptions to the untaxed motor fuel prohibition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(8)) and history note. Exempts eight categories from subsection 1: suppliers' in-state bulk transfer/terminal fuel, consumers' out-of-state tank fuel (excluding interstate users), dyed diesel, properly documented exports under sections 142.914 and 142.926, aircraft kerosene under section 142.815(1), refunded consumer fuel, government/tribal/reciprocity exempt fuel under section 142.815(2)(3)–(4) and section 142.617, and distributors meeting section 142.926 conditions.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor penalty and vehicle or cargo seizure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Classifies violating section 142.923 as a class A misdemeanor and subjects the vehicle and its cargo to impoundment and seizure.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 3 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(8) of sub 2) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified section 142.803 untaxed-fuel prohibition (qualified by sub 2 and section 142.929 distributor import compliance) in sub 1, eight cross-referenced exceptions (sections 142.914, 142.926, 142.815, and 142.617) in sub 2, and class A misdemeanor plus vehicle/cargo impoundment and seizure in sub 3. All 3 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Required dyed diesel and kerosene notices on shipping papers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Except as in subsection 3, requires transport truck shipping papers (in addition to section 142.914(1)) to bear exact statutory nontaxable-use and penalty notices for dyed diesel fuel and dyed kerosene loads or portions.

headings.title: When violation occurs upon boarding vehicle
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Specifies that a violation of subsection 1 occurs upon boarding the vehicle with a shipping paper failing to meet section 142.926 requirements.

headings.title: Advance notification procedure for noncompliant import shipping papers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants director discretion to provide an advance notification procedure when an importer cannot obtain compliant terminal-issued shipping papers for imported fuel.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for knowing violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Classifies any knowing violation of any part of section 142.926 as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Conveyance detention and seizure of undocumented fuel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') for the director, appointee, or representative to hold the transport conveyance and seize, confiscate, and dispose of motor fuel lacking the required shipping paper.

headings.title: Enforcement authority of director and highway patrol
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Grants full authority to enforce section 142.926 to the director, duly appointed agents, and the highway patrol and its officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 6 subsections and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified required dyed-diesel and dyed-kerosene notices (qualified by sub 3 and supplemental to section 142.914(1)) in sub 1, violation-upon-boarding timing in sub 2, discretionary advance notification for noncompliant imports in sub 3, knowing class A misdemeanor in sub 4, permissive conveyance detention and fuel seizure in sub 5, and director/highway patrol enforcement authority in sub 6. All 6 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: Pre-entry duties for importing undyed, tax-unpaid motor fuel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(5)) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Sets five pre-entry conditions for licensed distributors and transporters entering Missouri highways by loaded transport truck with out-of-state terminal fuel that is neither federally dyed nor tax-paid/accrued to the supplier: 24-hour import verification number, prominent indelible paper display, terminal origin and importer details, other required chapter paper data, and timely remittance of prior import-number taxes.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for knowing violations and good-faith limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Makes knowing violation or knowing aiding and abetting a class A misdemeanor, qualified by a fine-only limit for a first offense involving a good-faith belief that the distributor could import under the conditions. Revised during review to preserve the 'knowing' culpability requirement.

headings.title: Conveyance detention and seizure of undocumented fuel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') for the director, appointee, or representative to hold the transport conveyance and seize, confiscate, and dispose of motor fuel lacking the required shipping paper under section 142.929.

headings.title: Enforcement authority of director and highway patrol
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants full authority to enforce section 142.929 to the director, duly appointed agents, and the highway patrol and its officers.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(5) of sub 1) and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified five pre-entry duties for licensed distributors and transporters importing undyed, tax-unpaid out-of-state terminal fuel by loaded transport truck in sub 1, knowing class A misdemeanor with fine-only good-faith first-offense limit in sub 2, permissive detention/seizure in sub 3, and director/highway patrol enforcement in sub 4. Revised sub 2 title to preserve the 'knowing' mens rea qualification; retained subs 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Prohibition on highway vehicle operation with dyed fuel
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 2012 H.B. 1402 merged with S.B. 470). Prohibits operating or maintaining a motor vehicle on any Missouri public highway with chapter-dyed motor fuel in its fuel supply tank.

headings.title: Exceptions for out-of-state, federal-law, and state-of-emergency uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(3)) and history note. Exempts three categories from section 142.932: vehicles fueled in out-of-state jurisdictions permitting dyed highway fuel of that color/type, highway uses lawful under the Internal Revenue Code and chapter, and vehicles engaged in public safety matters or utility-service restoration (including public utilities, rural electric cooperatives, and contractors) during a gubernatorial state of emergency. Revised during review to avoid omitting public safety matters alongside utility restoration.

headings.title: Prohibition on selling or holding dyed fuel for taxable use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Bars selling or holding for sale dyed diesel fuel or dyed kerosene for a use the person knows or has reason to know is a taxable use (preserving archived phrasing 'taxable use of the diesel fuel').

headings.title: Prohibition on using or holding dyed diesel for taxable use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 3 by barring using or holding for use dyed diesel fuel (not referencing kerosene) for a taxable use when knowing or having reason to know it was dyed.

headings.title: Willfully altering fuel dye or marker to evade tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Prohibits willfully altering or attempting to alter, with intent to evade tax, the strength or composition of any dye or marker in dyed diesel fuel or dyed kerosene. Revised during review to capture the express 'intent to evade tax' element.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for knowing violations with intent to evade
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Classifies knowingly violating or knowingly aiding and abetting a violation of section 142.932 with intent to evade chapter tax as a class A misdemeanor.

headings.title: Joint and several liability matching 26 U.S.C. Section 6715
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Holds a person, business entity, and willfully participating officers, employees, or agents jointly and severally liable with the entity for state tax and penalties matching those imposed under 26 U.S.C. Section 6715 or its successor. Revised during review to replace 'under' with 'matching' so the heading does not imply direct federal imposition.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 7 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(3) of sub 2) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 2012 H.B. 1402 merged with S.B. 470), and verified all fingerprints. Verified highway dyed-fuel bar in sub 1, out-of-state/federal-law/gubernatorial state-of-emergency public-safety and utility-restoration exceptions in sub 2, distinct selling/holding dyed diesel or kerosene vs. using/holding dyed diesel prohibitions in subs 3–4, willful tax-evasion dye/marker alteration bar in sub 5, knowing tax-evasion class A misdemeanor in sub 6, and willful joint/several state liability matching 26 U.S.C. Section 6715 in sub 7. Revised titles for subs 2, 5, and 7 for scope, mens rea, and state-vs-federal precision; retained subs 1, 3, 4, and 6.

headings.title: Fuel sampling, facility and record inspections, and inspection sites
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (introductory clause and subdivisions (1)–(5), including definition of 'designated inspection site') and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 2014 S.B. 842). Authorizes credentialed inspectors (including federal employees and state contractors) to inspect without prior notice, take diesel coloration samples, search containers/equipment, and demand immediate production of transport shipping papers and records at non-exhaustive listed locations.

headings.title: Reasonable suspicion limit for non-seller, unlisted-site sampling
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note (A.L. 2014 S.B. 842). Notwithstanding subsection 1, bars diesel-coloration sampling inspections of individuals neither holding fuel for wholesale/retail sale nor located at listed sites unless inspectors have reasonable suspicion of chapter violations at the unlisted location. Revised during review to replace 'non-commercial' with 'non-seller' (matching 'not holding the fuel for wholesale or retail sale') and specify diesel sampling.

headings.title: Agencies and officers authorized to conduct inspections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes inspections by director's agents/appointees, the departments of public safety and agriculture, motor carrier inspectors, and other law enforcement officers under director procedures, conferring statutory personnel powers on director agents/appointees.

headings.title: Reasonable detention of fuel transporters for compliance checks
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Grants permissive authority ('may') to reasonably detain persons or equipment transporting fuel in or through Missouri only as long as necessary to determine compliance with chapter 142 and its rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 4 subsections (including subdivisions (1)–(5) and 'designated inspection site' definition in sub 1) and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, A.L. 2014 S.B. 842), and verified all fingerprints. Verified no-prior-notice diesel coloration sampling, container/equipment/record inspections, and non-exhaustive sites in sub 1, reasonable-suspicion limit for diesel coloration sampling of individuals not holding fuel for wholesale/retail sale at unlisted sites in sub 2, authorized agencies/officers in sub 3, and permissive necessary-duration transporter detention in sub 4. Revised sub 2 title to replace 'non-commercial' with 'non-seller' and specify sampling; retained subs 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Audit authority, assessment limit, and exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Authorizes auditing records, books, papers, and equipment of licensees or other persons selling, transporting, storing, or using motor fuel, and limits additional licensee tax assessments to three years after filing an erroneous report except in cases of fraud, neglect, or failure to file.

headings.title: Record availability at in-state locations or director's offices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires making records available during normal business hours at an in-state physical location, or at the director's offices within three business days of request if kept outside Missouri.

headings.title: Immediate on-site inspection and disclosure of shipping papers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes credentialed inspectors (including federal employees and state contractors) to inspect and requires fuel vendors, transporters, and bulk purchasers to immediately disclose chapter-required shipping papers maintained at the physical location.

headings.title: Civil penalty for refusing an authorized inspection or audit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Imposes a $5,000 civil penalty, in addition to other chapter penalties, on any person refusing a chapter-authorized inspection or audit.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for refusing inspection to evade tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 4 by making refusal to allow an inspection (text does not repeat 'or audit') for the purpose of evading tax a class A misdemeanor in addition to other chapter penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 5 subsections and history/effective-date notes (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99), and verified all fingerprints. Verified audit authority and three-year assessment limit with fraud/neglect/nonfiling exceptions in sub 1, in-state vs. three-business-day out-of-state record availability in sub 2, immediate on-site shipping-paper inspection/disclosure in sub 3, $5,000 civil penalty for refusing inspection or audit in sub 4, and class A misdemeanor for refusing an inspection (text omits 'or audit') to evade tax in sub 5. All 5 drafted titles retained as accurate.

headings.title: First lien on property and priority exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1998 S.B. 619, Effective 1-1-99). Creates a first lien on all real and personal property of the debtor for unpaid chapter tax, penalties, and interest, subordinated to state/county/municipal property tax liens and prior-attached rights of bona fide mortgagees, pledgees, judgment creditors, or purchasers.

headings.title: Filing, recording, and multi-county effect of lien notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires duplicate lien-notice filing with the delinquent assessment attached in the county of residence or principal place of business (recorded in land records and filed like chattel mortgages to impart notice), and permits like filings in any other county where the debtor owns property.

headings.title: Satisfaction of lien upon payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Directs the director, upon payment of assessed tax, penalty, and interest, to notify the recorder of deeds by registered or certified letter so the recorder marks the lien record satisfied with the date.

headings.title: Director's lien records and public disclosure on request
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires the director to maintain records of filed liens, filing dates, tax due, and satisfaction dates, and to furnish such information to any person upon request.
